title: L1-inception-jira-uploader Output — jira_upload_status
description: This agent's top-level envelope intentionally differs from the other 3 agents: it carries input_summary instead of a top-level status enum, and reports its own success/failure via content.items.agent_status. This is the confirmed, real-world shape for this specific agent — do not force it into the shared agent-output-schema.json's top-level 'status' field.

execution_id.description: Format exec-<uuid>. Freshly generated for this execution. May be 'exec-unavailable' only if the runtime could not supply one before a hard failure occurred.

workflow_execution_id.description: Inherited verbatim from the upstream AgentOutput's workflow_execution_id (originated by L1-inception-epics-creator). Never generated by this agent. May be 'wf-unavailable' only if no upstream id could be read before a hard failure occurred.

source_agent_ids.description: The upstream evaluator agents this run's inputs came from.

agent_status.description: 'success' if the tool invoked, zero failures, total_created == total_expected. 'partial_success' if some created and some failed. 'failed' if validation failed / tool not invoked / fatal error / zero created.

success.description: true only if the tool ran and returned >= 1 created issue, with no fatal error.

total_failed.description: Counts Jira-level issue creation failures ONLY (a payload was submitted to tool-L1-jira-upload-epics and it returned a 'Failed: ...' line for that issue). total_created + total_failed must equal total_expected in these cases. This is DISTINCT from failed_issues[] below: a pre-flight halt (e.g. upstream status != success, or zero valid epics after validation) means total_failed stays 0 (no Jira submission was ever attempted), yet failed_issues[] still carries exactly one synthetic entry describing the halt reason.

logical_id.description: e.g. EP-01 or F-01.1 — the input epic_id/feature_id this issue was created from.

jira_key.description: The real Jira issue key returned by the tool, e.g. GGMDEMOS-123.

failed_issues.description: Reports BOTH per-issue Jira creation failures (counted in issue_counts.total_failed) AND pre-flight halt reasons (upstream status != success, or zero valid epics after validation) which are NOT counted in total_failed since no Jira submission was ever attempted for those. A pre-flight halt always produces exactly one entry here even though total_failed remains 0.

error.description: Verbatim error detail — either the tool's 'Failed: ... | Detail: ...' line, the tool's 'Fatal error: ...' line, or an INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT explanation if the tool was never invoked.
